rules: Lead with the actual mobility intent and entity/route name.
Keep every landing title unique.
Do not append repetitive keyword variants.
Summarize the practical answer and user benefit.
Mention the origin/destination or place naturally.
Do not promise live timings unless rendered from live data.
Use the natural localized name and primary intent.
Do not mechanically repeat the SEO title.
Use H2/H3 to make each section understandable in isolation.
Prefer headings that reflect real visitor decisions or questions.
Answer the primary mobility question before background context.
Each Q&A answer must make sense if extracted without the rest of the page.
State entities, hubs and modes explicitly instead of relying on pronouns.
Do not create content solely to target AI systems.

selection: route landing that starts or ends at this entity
endpoint place pages for a route landing
one genuinely useful alternative route or nearby destination
avoid: linking every page in the same category
generic anchors such as click here or learn more
repeating the same target multiple times without user value

rules: Use questions a traveller could genuinely ask before or during the trip.
Do not create multiple near-identical keyword variants of the same question.
Start each answer with the useful conclusion, then add context.
Keep answers factual and stable; volatile information belongs to dynamic components.

sections.purpose: Identify the place and immediately answer how a visitor should think about reaching it.
Summarize meaningful modes/hubs and when each option is useful without freezing live timetable data.
Stable orientation, luggage, accessibility, walking or transfer advice.
Show relevant visitor fares from the central verified fare registry when price materially affects the choice.
Answer distinct high-intent visitor questions that are not already fully answered by the main blocks.
Only mobility-adjacent local context. Cultural/history depth stays in Unlock Venice editorial articles.
Link 2–4 genuinely connected transport landing pages.
Link 3–6 same-language Unlock Venice articles selected by editorial scoring.
State the origin/destination pair and immediately explain the main practical choices.
Compare meaningful transport modes by use case, transfers, walking and operational simplicity.
Give decision guidance for common traveller profiles without inventing a universally best option.
Stable luggage, transfer, accessibility, boarding or orientation advice.
Show relevant visitor fares from the central verified fare registry when price materially affects the choice.
Answer distinct route-specific questions such as transfers, walking, luggage or arrival point.
Explain the destination/interchange context only where it helps the onward journey.
Link endpoint landing pages plus 0–2 genuinely useful adjacent/alternative route pages.
Link 3–6 same-language Unlock Venice articles selected by editorial scoring.

rules: Show ordinary visitor fares when they materially help the travel decision.
Never copy fare numbers directly into narrative prose when the same value can come from the central fare registry.
Use 'da' for priceType=from and label third-party values as indicative.
Do not surface resident-only Venezia Unica fares in tourist guidance unless explicitly explained.
Display the last verification date and link to the source used for each fare group.
Price information is guidance, not a guarantee; users should verify before purchase.
